title: Grateful Dead Live at Various on 1966-03-12
source: Acid Test material, labelled with numbers 5,6 in supplement to previous 4 disc set.

ai_review.summary: Good-quality early‑era field recording of a rare 1966 Acid Test set, highlighted by a scorching Viola Lee Blues, soulful Next Time You See Me and Pigpen‑driven blues jams.
ai_review.review: The compilation captures an intriguing snapshot of the Dead’s first acid‑test performances – a blues‑heavy set bristling with early‑era energy, standout renditions of Viola Lee Blues, Next Time You See Me, Midnight Hour and vocal gems from Jerry and Bobby.  While the tape shows the usual hiss and occasional “garbage” noise of archival material, listeners repeatedly note its tight playing and historical significance.

ai_rating.rationale: Over twenty reviews overwhelmingly praise the music (standout early songs, strong Pigpen influence) and deem the recording worthwhile despite modest tape noise; the weight of consistent high stars yields a solid 4‑plus rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners describe the audio as tight and enjoyable for an archival field recording, noting some hiss/garbage noise but no major dropouts; overall listenable for its historical value.

standout_songs: Beat It On Down The Line (BIODTL)
One Kind Favor / See My Grave Is Kept Clean
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑era, blues‑focused set with strong Pigpen influence; the band moves fluidly through traditional numbers and originals, delivering high energy and soulful jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for unique licks in the opening minutes of "In The Midnight Hour" and strong vocal delivery on "It's A Sin" (and later praised for belting "Hey Little One").
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for choppier bass than later years but still providing a solid, driving rhythm that underpins the blues‑heavy set.
band_member_comments.Bob: Acknowledged for good singing on Beat It On Down The Line (BIODTL) and overall vocal contributions during the early material.
